traps.trap: Adhesions are the most common cause of obstruction everywhere, so they answer the Indian-setting 'most common cause' PYQ; Crohn's is assumed to be the common stricture in India (TR41 merged in)

probes.stem_idea: Same question restated: 'current practice, adult small bowel obstruction, abdominal surgery common' versus 'PYQ key'. Which pairing is right?
probes.correct: PYQ key: hernia; current practice: adhesions
distractor_set: PYQ key: adhesions; current practice: hernia
PYQ key: adhesions; current practice: adhesions

traps.trap: Adhesions explain obstruction in every adult, including the patient with no previous surgery

traps.trap: Intussusception is a childhood disease with an enema cure, so an adult is managed the same way

probes.note: the trap is the paediatric memory carried over without the age qualifier

probes.stem_idea: Why is adult intussusception managed differently from the child's: which statement explains it?

distractor_set: Adult bowel wall is too thick for the enema pressure
Adults never present with a mass

repair.strategy: E7: contrast child and adult side by side, naming the lead point

traps.retest: contrast probe in the paediatric segment and a vignette in the cold segment with age as the only clue.
traps.report_hint: avoided: you used age to choose the pathway. recovered: you now ask 'lead point?' for any adult. fell_open: adult intussusception means look for a tumour and resect.

traps.trap: Every intussusception, or every child, goes straight to theatre

traps.trap: The cardinal features follow the same timeline at every level of obstruction

probe_plan: Backbone traps: TR17 (derive cardinal features from the level of block), TR22 (recognise strangulation), TR23 (the 72-hour trial and what overrides it), TR31 (drip and suck first), TR5 (test ladder) and TR1 (PYQ key versus current practice). Meet them in this order: TR1 and TR40 early as the hook and causes segment (the exam key conflict frames the module); TR17 and TR18 in the clinical segment (E3 reversed-mechanism repair done by predict-then-show); TR11, TR12, TR8 and TR5 in the investigations segment, with TR11 and TR12 co-probed on one film stem; TR22 then TR31 then TR23 then TR26 in management, because strangulation recognition is the premise for the 72-hour rule and the timing numbers; TR2, TR13 and TR14 in a hernia mini-run (history qualifier, risk, eponyms); TR3 and TR4 as a paired child-versus-adult intussusception branch; TR21, TR35 and TR36 in the large bowel segment. Every trap's second probe returns in a later segment or the cold final segment in a different form; TR22, TR23 and TR31 should recur in the cold segment as unaided vignettes. Competing options inside stems: TR1/TR35/TR2 (most-common-cause stems), TR3/TR4 (enema versus resection), TR22/TR23/TR31 (strangulation, trial, resuscitation). Merged traps appear as extra distractors under their surviving ID; any distractor tagged to a dropped trap in a probe note is marked partial in the blueprint. The cap is 20; 21 traps dropped or merged. Unrefutable items in the brief were not branched.
